This
document lists the procedure details the minor maintenance activities (1st level
of maintenance as indicated by the P1), which must be performed from 1:2
years as indicated by the Y1:2. The first check is performed by MPIS Document #
T-009-r0, the daily check.

items:
Wear your safety helmet, safety shoes, safety 
 harness and use only fiberglass ladders.

Proper well fixed ladder should be used for climbing on top of the
 Transformer tank.

Wear your breathing mask before dry cleaning of bushings and earth point
 insulators.

While working at night ensure adquate lighting is provided for the entire
 work area.

Dielectric
 strength oil tester.

Oil
 sampling bottles and all equipment mentioned in MPIS document no.
 TD-SS-003-r0 for insulating oil sampling.

Reference
 thermometer and bath of water.

Spare
 parts for cooling equipment (oil pump, cooling fans, etc).

Sample
 and analyze gas taken from the insulating oil for main tank and tap-changer
 (see MPIS Document no. TB-SS-002-r0 insulating oil deterioration).

An
 initial inspection of the OLTC is required after the first 10,000 tap
 changes or one year from start of operation, whichever occurs first. After
 that, the interval between inspections should be increased to 30,000
 operation, or approximately 2 years.

Check
 the log for the average number of tap changes per day. The recommended
 maximum is 20.If the frequency of tap changes exceeds 30 per day,
 readjustment of the voltage- regulating relay may be necessary.

Check
 the breakdown voltage of the diverter switch insulating oil and the
 neutralization value of the oil. If in either case the insulating oil is
 found to have a breakdown voltage of < 40 KV/2.5mm, or a neutralization
 value > 0.3 mg KOH/g, replace the oil (see MPIS Document TB-SS-002-r0 for
 details).

Test
 the operation and accuracy of the indicator by inserting its sensing element
 into a bath of hot water and comparing operating temperatures with a
 reference thermometer Adjuster or replace the unit if any error is observed.

Check
 for moisture inside the back of the gauge, there should be no condensation
 or rust.

Check
 that all contacts, rubber fittings and the capillary tube on the indicator
 are in good condition.

Make
 sure that the alarm and trip contacts (if fitted) operate properly, clean or
 replace them if they do not.

When
 cleaning the dial cover do not use solvents such as ketones, thinner, and
 benzene, which may damage the cover.

Check
 that the gauge indicator shows the normal oil level, prescribed in the oil
 temperature graph on the nameplate near the main nameplate.

Clean
 the dial glass, or replace it if damaged.

Check
 that the alarm contacts are not closed.

Check
 that there is no oil leakage or rust.

Check
 that there is no oil leakage or parts damage. The indicator needle must
 point to FLOW, when the transformer pumps are operating.

General 
Cooling Equipment 
( Oil Pumps, Cooling Fans, Radiators, for example if installed )

items:
Check
 that the oil pumps are operating and have no oil leakage or abnormal noise.
 If any abnormal noise is heard, most likely the oil pump bearings need
 replacing.

Check
 that the cooling fans operate smoothly and create no abnormal noise or
 vibration.

If
 any abnormal noise is heard, it is very likely that the fan bearings need
 replacing.

Check
 for excessive buildup of grime on the radiator surfaces and clean it.

sections.text:
Water 
Cooled ( Cooling Equipment, if installed )

items:
Check
 that there is no water leakage or rust on the exterior, if necessary,
 disassemble the cooler as instructed in the instruction manual supplied with
 the transformer and inspect the interior for rust, corrosion, oil and water
 leakage and other problems.

Introduction

Safety
